purpose: A bounded, direct-task cancellation contract for the async APIs used by the current ecosystem. It is independent of the frozen TaskHandle lifecycle v2 contract and does not qualify general structured cancellation.
supported_scope: a move-only TaskHandle<T> receives one cooperative task_cancel request
a direct await observes one child terminal outcome; await? represents an observed child or current-task cancellation as Option::None
cold cancellation and cold-handle drop run frame cleanup before canceled terminal publication
whole-place, direct-field, and fixed-array-index cede frame locals are covered by the named cancellation redlines
Timer and TCP read suspension points observe task_cancel and clean up frame resources and reactor registrations without subsequent user code execution
direct Context Canceler.call() returns a domain cancellation error and allows caller to continue with buffer and listener ownership intact

guarantees.statement: task_cancel is a cooperative request: it is observable at the current supported suspension boundary and never fabricates a normal result.
At a direct await? boundary, canceled child completion or an observed current-task cancellation yields Option::None.
A cold cancellation or cold-handle drop runs frame-owned cleanup exactly once before canceled terminal publication.
The named direct-field and fixed-array-index cede redlines release every covered live resource exactly once after cancellation.
Once a direct normal-result claim has been established, a later cancellation request does not revoke that already-visible normal delivery.

On a supported Timer suspension boundary without Context Canceler involvement, a task_cancel request is observed; the task is woken and driven to terminal completed-canceled, timer token is invalidated, no subsequent CFG is executed, frame locals are dropped exactly once, and timer expiry causes no resumption.

On a supported TCP read suspension boundary on POSIX platforms without Context Canceler involvement, a task_cancel request is observed; the task is woken and driven to terminal completed-canceled, WaitRegistry and OS reactor subscriptions are deleted such that ready events are silenced, no subsequent CFG is executed, and frame locals are dropped exactly once.

When a raw TCP read or accept operation is canceled via direct Canceler.call() while the task itself is not cancel-requested, the operation returns the propagated cancellation error, caller control flow continues with ownership of the raw buffer or same listener instance intact, and canceler token count returns to baseline.

ecosystem_evidence.statement: A canceled Redis pool waiter returns a domain pool error without acquiring a lease.
A canceled PostgreSQL pool waiter returns a domain pool error without acquiring a lease.

explicitly_deferred: TLS cancellation paths across handshake, read, and write
Context deadline timeout error propagation (deferred to dedicated qualification)
owner-carrying async buffer restitution (e.g. read_into_async_context returning owned buffer on cancel)
concurrent dual-source cancellation (simultaneous task_cancel and Context Canceler.call)
TaskScope close, cancellation propagation, and cancel-join-drain progress
race2, select2, and any multi-source cancellation/loser-drain guarantee
borrowed scoped tasks and task values carrying PAL dependencies
dynamic projections, slices, arbitrary nested aggregates, and other unlisted async cede cleanup paths
graduation_requirements: Qualify direct-await and single-task I/O cancellation at one candidate revision without relying on TaskScope or race2 semantics.
Verify timer logical invalidation, TCP OS-level reactor silence, and same-listener context reuse.
Re-run every named source, native, and ecosystem evidence item from one clean candidate revision.
Record the result under candidate conformance output; do not mutate TaskHandle lifecycle v2 history.
